Unlike Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), which uses a single monolithic implicit function for the entire scene, NSVF partitions space into voxels, each containing a local implicit function mapping a point and ray direction to color and density [S3, S5, unofficial].

The claim states that unlike NeRF, which uses a single monolithic implicit function, NSVF partitions space into voxels, each containing a local implicit function mapping a point and ray direction to color and density. Source [S3] explicitly states: 'NSVF defines a set of voxel-bounded implicit fields... where each voxel contains an implicit function mapping a point and ray direction to color and density. This contrasts with NeRF, which uses a single implicit function for an entire scene.' Source [S5] corroborates this by describing NSVF as modeling a scene as a set of voxel-bounded implicit functions and defining the field for a point inside a voxel as outputting color and density based on voxel embedding and ray direction. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
*   Pass the concatenated embedding through a shared Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to predict volumetric density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$ [S1][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the concatenated embedding is passed through a shared MLP to predict volumetric density and color. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Feature representations were obtained by interpolating learnable features stored at voxel vertices, which were then processed by a shared MLP that computed σ and c.' Source [S3] confirms this by defining the implicit function as $F_{theta}^i: (g_i (mathbf{p}) , mathbf{v}) rightarrow (mathbf{c}, sigma)$, where $g_i(mathbf{p})$ is the representation (embedding) derived from the voxel vertices. Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
